review_scope: Manual inspection of all 17 frames plus frames 1, 9, and 17 from base, step-50, step-100, and step-200 under identical inference settings.

observations.base: Generated a colorful cylindrical object rather than a recognizable architectural building, with little useful rotational motion.
observations.step-50: Generated a grayscale cylindrical high-rise form, confirming that the architectural-domain signal was learned, but the object remained nearly static and undersized in frame.
observations.step-100: Generated a centered gray building mass with the clearest continuous viewpoint change and the most stable geometry among the tested checkpoints. Fine architectural detail and texture remain limited.
observations.step-200: Generated an elongated, low-detail building block. Motion remained visible, but proportions and appearance degraded compared with step-100, indicating over-training at the current learning rate.
observations.temporal_motion: Step-100 provides the best balance of architectural appearance, smooth viewpoint progression, stable framing, and geometric consistency.

conclusion: The 200-video pilot validates that the LoRA can learn the building domain and rotational video prior. It does not yet demonstrate missing-region completion, and training beyond step 100 degrades geometry under the current settings.
decision: Select step-100.safetensors as the current best checkpoint. Do not select the final checkpoint automatically. Use earlier validation and a lower learning rate in the next experiment before scaling to the full training split.
